title: How many dots after the second ring?
description: A hexagon cluster has a centre dot and a ring of six dots. The video adds the next ring of twelve dots to get nineteen, and Keeko's doubt, that every ring has six dots, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a cluster grows by adding a ring, and each new ring goes around the whole cluster, so it is longer than the one before. Watch for students who think every ring has the same number of dots.

source: A hexagon cluster has a centre dot and one ring of 6 dots. H
video_script.why: The child adds a longer ring around a cluster of dots and counts the dots in all.
video_script.substitution: The dots in a cluster are the dots already there plus the dots of the new ring.
video_script.anchor: a hexagon cluster of one centre dot and one ring of six dots, with a dotted outline for the next ring around it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says every ring has six dots, because the first ring has six. The next ring goes around the first ring, so it is longer, and it has twelve dots. The doubt is struck.
maths_rules: the centre dot and the first ring make 1 + 6 = 7 dots
slip: a ring that goes around a bigger cluster has more dots than the ring inside it
video_script.design: One idea: add the new ring to the dots already there. Assumes adding. Wrong idea: every ring has six dots. The cluster stays on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a hexagon cluster with one centre dot and a ring of 6 dots, and a dotted outline for the next ring

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.cluster: the centre dot and the ring of six dots appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a cluster of dots.
<bookmark mark='cluster'/>It has a centre dot and one ring of six dots.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>A bigger ring of twelve dots is added. How many dots are there then?

beats.on_screen: the cluster holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a centre dot, then a small ring around it, then a larger ring around both

marks.rings: a small ring appears around it, then a larger ring around both

narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>A cluster grows by adding a ring of dots all the way around it.
<bookmark mark='rings'/>A ring around a bigger cluster has more dots. The dots in all are the old dots plus the new ring.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 centre dot, a ring of 6 dots, a next ring of 12 dots
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one centre dot, a ring of six dots and a next ring of twelve dots.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of dots after the next ring

marks.find: the words number of dots are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of dots after the next ring is added.

marks.now: the centre dot and the ring of six are counted together

narration: <bookmark mark='now'/>Step one, count the cluster as it is. It has the centre dot and the first ring.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>One plus six is seven dots.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, add the next ring: 7 + 12 = 19 dots

marks.ring: the ring of twelve dots is drawn around the cluster

narration: <bookmark mark='ring'/>Step two, add the next ring. It has twelve dots and goes around the whole cluster.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Seven plus twelve is nineteen dots.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the cluster with the inner ring and the outer ring outlined in different colours; the bubble is struck through

marks.outer: the outer ring is outlined and its dots are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks every ring has six dots, because the first ring has six.
<bookmark mark='outer'/>But the next ring goes around the first ring, so it is longer. It has twelve dots.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Each new ring goes around a bigger cluster, so it needs more dots.
